summary: Heinrich Plütschau was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied theology at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1702 to 1704, where he also held an academic post.

Heinrich Rickert worked in philosophy, studying at Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1884–1885) and the University of Strasbourg (circa 1885–1888). He held posts at the University of Freiburg (circa 1891–1916) and Heidelberg University (circa 1916–1932).

Heinrich Rückert was a scholar in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He held academic posts at the University of Jena from circa 1845 to 1852 and at the University of Breslau from circa 1852 to 1875.

Heinrich Schenkl studied at the University of Vienna from circa 1877 to 1882. He later held posts at the University of Graz from circa 1892 to 1917 and at the University of Vienna from circa 1917 to 1919.
Heinrich Schliemann worked in the fields of history and archaeology. He pursued studies at the University of Paris between 1866 and 1868, and at the University of Rostock in circa 1869.

Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Zurich and Berlin under Bernhard Hirzel, Karl Lachmann, and others. He held multiple positions at the University of Zurich, including full professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics from 1864 to 1889.

Indologist Heinrich Stönner studied at Marburg, Berlin (under Karl Friedrich Geldner, Albrecht Weber, and Emil Sieg), and Halle-Wittenberg (PhD under Richard Pischel). He held positions at Berlin State Museums and the Ethnological Museum of Berlin.

Heinrich Uhle was an Indologist who studied under Hermann Brockhaus at the University of Leipzig, earning his Dr. phil. between circa 1864 and 1868. He served as a classical languages teacher at Kreuzschule from 1868 to 1911.

Heinrich Wenzel specialized in Indology and Tibetology, studying at Jena, Tübingen (PhD under Rudolf von Roth), Strasbourg, Leipzig, and Oxford. He completed his Habilitation at Leipzig under Georg von der Gabelentz and held a post there in 1887.

Heinrich Zimmer worked in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy, studying at Strasbourg, Tübingen, and Berlin under scholars including Rudolf von Roth and Albrecht Weber. He held posts at Berlin, Greifswald, Heidelberg, Columbia University, and Balliol College, Oxford.

Heinrich von Stietencron studied at Munich (under Helmut Hoffmann), SOAS, and Heidelberg. An Indologist and religious studies scholar, he worked as an assistant at Heidelberg before serving as chairholder at the University of Tübingen from 1973 to 1998.
Heinrich von Wlislocki was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied under Sámuel Brassai at Franz Joseph University, earning his Ph.D. there between 1875 and 1879.

Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar Heinz Bechert earned his PhD at Munich under Helmut Hoffmann and completed a doctorate at Mainz. He held posts at Saarland, Mainz, and served as Chair of Indology at the University of Göttingen (1965–2000).

Linguist Heinz Kronasser studied at the University of Vienna under Paul Kretschmer and Erich Frauwallner, and earned his Ph.D. at Graz. He held academic posts at Graz, the University of Vienna, and the University of Würzburg.
Heinz Kucharski was a scholar of Indology who studied at the University of Hamburg in 1938. He served as Director of the Indian Department at the Grassi Museum of Ethnology from circa 1958 to 1984.

Heinz Mode specialized in Indology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, studying at Berlin, Colombo, Visva-Bharati, and Basel. He served as Professor of Oriental Archaeology at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from 1948 to 1978.

Specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, Heinz Zimmermann studied at Zurich, Freiburg, and Basel (Ph.D. 1958–1967). He taught at the University of Zurich (1971–1979) and served as professor of Sanskrit at the University of Lausanne (1977; 1981).

Heleen De Jonckheere is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who completed her doctorate at Ghent University (2016–2020). She held posts at the University of Chicago, University of Toronto Mississauga, and SOAS University of London.

Helen Baroni works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied at Grinnell College, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Columbia University under Paul B. Watt, and has held a post at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa since circa 1993.

Helen Hardacre specializes in Japanology and religious studies, having studied at Vanderbilt and Chicago under Joseph M. Kitagawa and Jonathan Z. Smith. She held posts at Princeton University, Griffith University, and Harvard University.
